subject: scenario-viola-run-start-sequence-to-child-spawn
origin: ## 4. Span / Trace Coverage › #### Scenario: `viola run` start sequence to child spawn
text: - **Must-trace spans:** `run.start` (INTERNAL, root) › `run.collision_check` › `run.pin_copy` › `run.conpty_sideload` (Windows) › `run.version_gate` (spawns the `version-probe`) › `channel.bind` › `run.budget_eval` (INTERNAL, `trigger="start"`; its attributes are under Scenario: Budget governor; chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor) › `state.snapshot_write` › `state.heartbeat_start` › `pty.spawn` (CLIENT). Two start steps carry no span and no log line, by design (the operator's answer at the chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through wrap; that chunk's plan added no span name): the statusline source read, whose result is the snapshot's `statusline_command`, and the settings override write (`instances/<name>/settings.json` through `replace_private`, Unix only), which sits between the first snapshot and `pty.spawn`. The child's `--settings` argument, the source path and the command appear in no line or span. A third start step carries none either, as landed (chunk 2026-10-10-session-links): the link set's restore, one read pass over the instance's `events.ndjson` through `viola_state::events::read_from`, made beside the wait feed's rebuild and before the endpoint serves. It appends nothing and logs nothing, its result is the first snapshot's `links`, and the start appends no record for links, so the span chain above and the product order below are unchanged; `viola revive` starts through the same function.

subject: scenario-viola-run-start-sequence-to-child-spawn
origin: ## 4. Span / Trace Coverage › #### Scenario: `viola run` start sequence to child spawn
text:
- **Required log fields:**
  - Common fields with `process="run"` and `corr` null.
  - `process-start{subject:"self", service_name, version, os, pid, endpoint_kind}`.
  - `process-start` / `process-exit{subject:"version-probe", child_exit_status, duration_ms}`.
  - On failure, `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail}` with `detail` ∈ `already-live|squatted-name|pinned-hash-mismatch|batch-script-child` (Founder Direction 4; no path or pid). `viola revive` enters the same sequence through the same start, after an instance check that precedes the log init and writes no line when it refuses, then a preflight of its own whose refusals add `detail` ∈ `no-session|session-live|cwd-missing` (and `already-live`, from the same collision check) before any child is started; its `session-live` reading (skipped under `--fork`) writes one `process-start` / `process-exit{subject:"agents-probe"}` pair in `run-<name>.ndjson`, plus one `parse-rejected{parser:"claude-agents-json"}` on an oversize or malformed answer, and passes on a failed read; a revive that passes its preflight runs `run.collision_check` twice, once in the preflight and once inside the start.
  - On success, `process-start{subject:"claude-child", child_pid, pty_backend, cli_version, cli_verified, env_stripped_count, env_stripped_known, env_kept}` (D-34), plus, on Windows when the `run.conpty_sideload` outcome is not `loaded`, `sideload_fallback` (`hash-mismatch|unreadable|load-failed|not-built`, D-36). A degraded sideload adds no `process-exit{exit_code:1}` and no panic line.
  - In `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, `pty_backend` is `{ "type": "string" }`, while `sideload_fallback` is closed in the `process-start` properties to `hash-mismatch|unreadable|load-failed|not-built` (`diag-detail.v1.json` carries neither). A sideload degrade is recorded on the existing info-level lines, never at `warn`, and no companion path or hash reaches a home-level line (D-36).
  - Product order `wheel{cause:"start"}` → `budget-gate` → `session-start` is verified from `events.ndjson` through `agent-run logs --kind`, not duplicated into process logs (`run` writes the first two; `session-start{source:"hook"}` is record three, sent by `viola hook` through `hook.event` since "Hooks to normalised events"; the harness `boot` readiness stage `start_records` checks `events.ndjson` lines 1-3 — `wheel{cause:"start"}` → `budget-gate` → `session-start{source:"hook"}` — with the missing code `<name>:events`).

subject: scenario-confirmed-send-cl-1-from-driver-to-readback
origin: ## 4. Span / Trace Coverage › #### Scenario: Confirmed `send` (CL-1) from driver to readback
text: - **Must-trace spans:** `send.client` (CLIENT; `cli` or `mcp.tool_call`) › `channel.request` (CLIENT) → `channel.dispatch` (SERVER, `run`) › `run.readiness_gate` › `pty.paste_write` › `run.confirm_window`. An unconfirmable send ends at `pty.paste_write` and opens no `run.confirm_window`. In the hook process: `hook.handle` › `channel.request(hook.event)`, the user-prompt-submit hook for an ordinary send and the session-start hook for a `/clear` confirmed by its new session or a `/compact` confirmed by its same session (verified CLI). One operation on this path carries no span and no line of its own, as landed (chunk 2026-10-10-session-links): the implicit link record (E3 below). After the second wheel and running-turn reads and directly before the send is issued, a `send` whose `from` is a name other than the wrapper's own records the link, so a new pair's `link` product line stands directly before that send's `send-issued` in `events.ndjson`, whose `cursor` is still the offset its own line starts at; a send refused at any earlier rung, one with no `from` and one under the wrapper's own name record nothing. A record that fails answers `-32603` with nothing issued and nothing typed, so no `send-issued` is written. `driver` and `driven` reach no process-log line.

origin: ## 4. Span / Trace Coverage › #### Scenario: Confirmed `send` (CL-1) from driver to readback
text: - **Cleanup:** `run.confirm_window` closes on the confirmation its send waits for, or on window expiry. For an ordinary send that is the matching `prompt-submitted{origin:"driver"}`. For a listed local command with a new-session post-condition on a verified CLI (`/clear`) it is the `session-start` whose `cause` is `clear` and whose `agent_session_id` is a string that differs from the id the send slot remembers; that send waits for its post-condition only, and no `prompt-submitted` claims it. For a listed local command with a compacted-session post-condition on a verified CLI (`/compact`) it is the `session-start` whose `cause` is `compact` and whose `agent_session_id` is a string equal to the id the send slot remembered before that line (nothing remembered claims nothing), no `prompt-submitted` claiming it either; its window is `COMPACT_CONFIRM_WINDOW` (40 s, PROVISIONAL), every other confirmed send's `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK` (10 s). Expiry is `send-refused{detail:"no-prompt-submitted"}` for all three (no new detail). An unconfirmable send (a listed command with no post-condition, or any listed command on an unverified CLI) opens no `run.confirm_window`. `channel-response` is emitted from a `Drop` guard in `channel.dispatch`, so an early return or error still logs it. `send.client` closes with `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code}` (0 / 10 / 11 / 12 / 13 / 14 / 20 / 21, or 1 `internal-error` on a reply with neither a parseable `result` nor an `error.code`); exit 20 carries `detail:"wrapper-fault"`, and exit 21 `detail:"instance-dead"` with `during` `connect` (no live snapshot, or the connect failed) or `call` (the connection lost after it).

subject: scenario-dialog-answer-question-permission-plan-including-the-unverified-cli-branch
origin: ## 4. Span / Trace Coverage › #### Scenario: Dialog → `answer` (question / permission / plan), including the unverified-CLI branch
text: - **Must-trace spans:** `hook.handle` (SERVER) › `channel.request(hook.dialog)` → `channel.dispatch` › `run.dialog_register` › `run.dialog_await` › `hook.decision_emit`. Driver side: `answer.client` › `channel.request(answer)` → `channel.dispatch`. One operation on the driver side carries no span and no line of its own, as landed (chunk 2026-10-10-session-links): the implicit link record in the wrapper's `answer` handling (E3 below). Once every refusal has passed and the response's kind matched the pending dialog, and before the `dialog-answered` line and the answer being taken, an `answer` whose `from` is a name other than the wrapper's own records the link (one `link` product line for a new pair, none for a pair the set holds); a refused answer, one with no `from` and one under the wrapper's own name record nothing. A record that fails answers `-32603`: the answer is not taken, the dialog stays held and no `dialog-answered` line is written.

origin: ## 4. Span / Trace Coverage › #### Scenario: Dialog → `answer` (question / permission / plan), including the unverified-CLI branch
text: - **Cleanup:** `run.dialog_await` closes on an answer, a hand-back or the hold's end. At the hold's end the wrapper appends one `dialog-expired{dialog_id, dialog_kind}` product line (`source: wrapper`, no question, plan or tool text; it wakes a parked `wait`) and writes one `dialog-answered{corr:<dialog_id>, dialog_kind, deadline_hit:true, duration_ms}` with no `from`; the reply stays `null`, so the hook writes `hook-decision{decision_emitted:false, deadline_hit:false}`, exits 0 with empty stdout, and the dialog renders for the human. A hand-back or an answer writes neither, and a failed append changes nothing else. The hook writes `deadline_hit:true` only when its own read times out at its backstop bound, `DIALOG_HOLD_MAX + 5 s` (3605 s). Fail-open before `dialog_id` gives `hook-invoked{corr:null}` + `hook-decision{corr:null, detail}` (Section 6 fail-open codes).
